subject: quick question on the cap table
ask: Wants 20 minutes about the cap table — second time asking in five days.
why: This is the most important message in the inbox and it looks like the least important. Priya went quiet for eleven weeks, then wrote twice in five days, both times calling it quick, both times at night. Nobody asks about their cap table twice for a small reason. The likely subject is a co-founder departure or a bridge she does not want to put in writing.
red_flags: Eleven weeks of silence before this
excerpt:
Hey — sorry to bug you again. Any chance of 20 min this week? Just a quick question on the cap table, nothing urgent. Would rather talk than email it.

P.
draft_reply:
Priya — how about tomorrow 8am or 4pm ET, your pick? Happy to make it longer than 20 if useful.

And whatever it is, it's fine to say it in the meeting rather than writing it down. Just tell me what you need.

subject: Re: seed round — timing
ask: Needs a yes or no before Thursday — a competing term sheet expires then.
why: Hard deadline attached to a live partner-review decision. The reply does not have to be a decision, but it has to be a real timeline, and it has to go today. Silence past Wednesday is read as a pass by any founder with another offer in hand.
excerpt:
No pressure intended and I'd much rather work with you than them — but I do have to give the other fund an answer by Thursday. Is there any read you can give me before then, even a directional one?

Sasha
draft_reply:
Sasha — you'll have a real answer from us by end of day Wednesday, not Thursday. That's a commitment.

Directionally: we're engaged, the open question for us is round construction rather than conviction in you. I'd rather tell you that plainly than have you read a delay as a signal.

subject: Series B — would love your help on two intros
ask: Wants intros to Series B funds — sent a list of nine names to choose from.
why: Portfolio founder raising, asking for the one thing that costs real relationship capital. Worth answering fast and narrowly: two strong intros beat nine weak ones, and sending all nine would spend credibility that gets her nothing.
excerpt:
Attaching the list we've built — nine funds, ranked. If any of these are people you know well I'd rather have your intro than go in cold. Totally understand if the answer is one or none.

Amara
draft_reply:
Amara — two of the nine I know well enough for the intro to actually carry weight, and I'll make both this week. The rest I'd be doing you a disservice on; a lukewarm intro is worse than a cold email you write yourself, which you're good at.

Sending the forwardable blurb tonight for you to edit before I send anything.

needs_decision.question: Which two of Amara's nine target funds get a personal intro?
options: Two, and offer to review her cold outreach for the rest
needs_decision.recommendation: Two, and offer to review her cold outreach for the rest
needs_decision.why: Intro capital is the scarcest thing here and it does not scale. Two intros that carry weight plus a genuinely useful edit pass on the other seven is more valuable to her than nine forwards that all read as obligation.
needs_decision.cost_of_delay: She is running a timed process. An intro that arrives after her first meetings is worth a fraction of one that arrives before.

subject: one for you — infra, seed, moving quickly
ask: Sending a new company and offering a double opt-in intro.
why: Dana is the highest-conversion source in the network — three deals in twelve months, two reached diligence. She sends few and sends well, so the reply cost is low and the expected value is high. Answer within the day even if the answer is not now.
excerpt:
Not going to oversell this one. Founder is technical, market is crowded, but she's the sharpest person I've met on the problem this year. Want me to make the intro or shall I hold?

D.
draft_reply:
Yes to the intro — your hit rate has earned an automatic yes at this point.

One thing before you send: is she running a process with a close date, or is this exploratory? Changes how fast I need to move and I'd rather know now than find out in the first call.

subject: Annual meeting — dates, and one question on Fund V pacing
ask: Confirming annual meeting dates and asking why Fund V deployment slowed in Q2.
why: An LP asking about pacing is never only asking about pacing. The scheduling half can be delegated; the pacing question needs a real answer from a partner and should not be bundled into a calendar reply.
red_flags: Two questions in one message — one delegable, one not
excerpt:
Two things. First, we're firming up dates for the annual — does the week of Oct 19 work on your end?

Second, and no rush on this one: we noticed Fund V pacing looked lighter in Q2 than the prior two quarters. Nothing alarming, just want to understand the thinking.

Beth
draft_reply:
Beth — week of Oct 19 works; sending three specific slots separately so we can lock it.

On pacing: the slowdown was deliberate rather than a lack of opportunity. Happy to walk you through what we passed on in Q2 and why — that's a more useful conversation than the number itself. Would 30 minutes before the annual be helpful, or would you rather have it in writing first?

subject: Re: reference calls — two design partners confirmed
ask: Confirming two design-partner references for Wednesday and asking who should join.
why: Logistics on a live diligence thread. No partner judgment required to schedule it; the judgment is in what gets asked on the call, which is already drafted in the deal's diligence brief.
excerpt:
Both are up for it — Wednesday works for either 11am or 3pm ET. Let me know which and I'll send invites. Happy to be on or off the call, your preference.

Kwame
draft_reply:
Wednesday 11am works, and better if you're not on it — references are more useful when the founder isn't in the room, and that's not a comment on you.

We'll come back same day either way.

subject: Re: apparel manufacturing at the A
ask: Open to looking at an apparel-manufacturing Series A and asking what stage the company is at.
why: This is the other half of Amara's intro request arriving before it was asked for. Answering this well is what makes that intro land, so the two should be handled as one move rather than two threads.
excerpt:
Always happy to look. We've been under-allocated in vertical software for manufacturing and I've been trying to fix that. What stage are they at — post-A metrics or pre?

Hiro
draft_reply:
Post-A metrics, raising a B. I'll send the forwardable blurb this week once the founder has signed off on it.

Short version so you can decide whether to keep reading: production planning for small apparel manufacturers, four years in, and the founder is the reason to take the meeting.

subject: Pendle Health — seed round, prior auth for specialty practices
ask: Cold pitch for a $2.5M seed, asking for 30 minutes.
why: Cold, credible, and scored a 5. Real pain and a real founder, but the go-to-market is one practice at a time with no evidence yet that it compounds. Worth a screen, not worth a partner's Monday. Booked for Thursday.
excerpt:
We handle prior authorisation end to end for specialty practices — currently 11 clinics, $18K MRR, growing through referrals between practice managers. Raising $2.5M. Would love 30 minutes.

Elena Vos, Pendle Health
draft_reply:
Elena — thanks for the clear note; the referral-between-practice-managers detail is the most interesting line in it.

Booking 30 minutes Thursday. Fair warning that the thing I'll push hardest on is whether that referral motion compounds or whether every clinic is its own sale. Worth thinking about before we talk.

subject: Keynote invitation — Northeast Founders Summit, November
ask: Wants a 40-minute keynote in Boston on Nov 12, plus a panel the same afternoon.
why: Real event, decent audience, but a full day plus travel for a November slot. This is a calendar-shape question rather than a judgment question — the answer depends on what else November already holds, which is the assistant's to answer first.
red_flags: Two commitments bundled as one ask
excerpt:
We'd be honoured to have you open the summit. 40 minutes, topic of your choosing, and we'd love you on the afternoon founder panel as well if the day allows.

Grace Lassiter
draft_reply:
Grace — thank you for asking. Checking what November looks like before I answer properly.

If it happens it will be the keynote or the panel rather than both; a half day I can protect, a full one I probably can't.

subject: Re: our conversation
ask: Thanking us for the pass note and the two intros; says both funds replied.
why: A pass that produced a warmer relationship than the meeting did. Nothing needed beyond a short human reply, but worth noting: this is the outcome the pass-note habit exists to produce, and the counter should be visible somewhere.
excerpt:
Genuinely the most useful no I've had in this raise — both intros replied within a day and one is now in diligence. Whatever the next one is, you'll see it first.

Theo
draft_reply: Theo — glad they were useful, and I meant what I said about the shape rather than the team. Send the next one early.

subject: Quick question, {FirstName}
ask: Wants 15 minutes to demo a data platform.
why: Untargeted mass template — the unrendered merge tag in the subject line settles it. No reply warranted, and it is the fourth from this sender this quarter.
red_flags: Fourth message from this sender this quarter
No indication they know what the firm does
excerpt:
Hi {FirstName}, noticed you're in the investment space and thought DataBridge could be a great fit for your workflows. Do you have 15 minutes Thursday?

Trent

subject: Coffee chat request — breaking into VC
ask: MBA student asking for 30 minutes about getting into venture.
why: Polite, well-written, and one of roughly nine of these a week. Batched to Friday with a real reply rather than ignored — the answer is a link to something written once and a genuine no to the meeting.
excerpt:
I know your time is valuable so I'll be brief — I'm a second-year MBA focused on early-stage software and would be grateful for 30 minutes of your perspective on breaking in.

Camila Ruiz
draft_reply:
Camila — I can't do the 30 minutes, and I'd rather tell you that than let it sit in a folder for three weeks.

What I'd actually suggest: the people who broke in that I've watched do it did so by publishing a point of view on a specific market until someone in it noticed. That is slower and works better than a hundred coffees. Happy to read the first one you write.
